title: Cognitive Function, Air Quality, and Built Environment among Rural Residents at Risk for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
text: Rural communities experiencing repeated intermittent exposures to air pollution during agricultural burns often face social isolation, and both are linked to increased risk for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias (ADRD). However, the intersection of these factors, combined with the influence of rural built and social environments on cognitive function has not been studied, particularly in the context of broadly representative farm workers who already face increased ADRD risk. This proposed research will inform the design of public health interventions that can diminish the threat of ADRD in rural settings and save healthcare dollars.

title: Geographically-Explicit Ecological Momentary Assessment Protocol to Assess the Linkages Between Intersectional Discrimination and CVD Risk Among Sexual and Gender Minorities
text:
Stress during young adulthood contributes to harmful health behaviors such as poor
sleep, smoking, alcohol use, and physical inactivity, which increase the risk of early
chronic disease. This project uses innovative real-time methods to understand how
stress is experienced in everyday environments and how social supports can reduce its
harmful effects. Findings will guide the development of tailored prevention strategies to
improve the health of young adults and reduce long-term cardiometabolic disparities.

title: Building a Systems Immunopeptidomics Framework to Challenge the Current T Cell Activation Paradigm
text:
The human immunopeptidome, consisting of thousands of cell surface peptides, is crucial for T cells to
distinguish 'self' from 'nonself' (foreign invaders). Traditionally thought to be ignored by T cells in most tissues,
we propose that self-peptides collectively influence T cell activation to fight threats. We will build an innovative
systems immunopeptidomics framework to demonstrate the regulatory power of the self-immunopeptidome
within the organism, which may radically shift our understanding of the immune system, lead to new therapies,
and lay the foundation for a Human Immunopeptidome Project.

title: Sequence, chromatin, and cellular contexts of transcription factor- DNA interaction and function
text:
Transcription factor - DNA interactions and their regulatory outcomes are governed by multiple layers of
contextual information in the cell, shaping gene expression programs essential for growth, development, and
stress responses. Our proposed research will investigate how changes in these contexts, including TF protein
sequences, DNA regulatory elements, chromatin accessibility, and cellular environments, collectively influence
TF binding and gene regulatory networks. The insights and predictive models we generate will enhance our
ability to study and interpret regulatory variants in complex diseases and support the development of precision
medicine strategies.

title: Light Activated Immunomodulation and in situ Scaffolding to Enhance MSC Therapy
text:
Human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) show great promise for tissue repair, regeneration, and the
treatment of various immune-related and neurodegenerative diseases. However, their clinical application
remains limited by immune rejection and poor engraftment. This project aims to develop a convenient and
effective light-activated hydrogel platform to enhance hMSC-based therapy. The findings will address a critical
knowledge gap and may advance the broader application of hMSC therapies.

title: Utilizing biochemical and functional genomic approaches to uncover key host invasion receptors in Plasmodium vivax
text:
The proposed research will provide insights into the molecular mechanisms by which Plasmodium vivax
parasites interact with red blood cells. I will identify the host receptors essential for the invasion of P. vivax into
the youngest of red blood cells, known as reticulocytes, to inform the development of anti-P. vivax
therapeutics.

title: Multi-scale consequences of variants in the schizophrenia risk gene SETD1A in a population isolate.
text:
Rare variants in SETD1A are associated with dramatically increased risk for schizophrenia, but
the clinical phenotype and cellular mechanisms are poorly understood. We will investigate
cognitive and psychiatric symptom phenotypes for carriers of SETD1A variants enriched in a
founder population, the Old Order Amish. We will study pluripotent stem cells derived form a
subset of these individuals to characterize variant  cell  brain  disease mechanisms.

title: Epigenetic mechanisms of inflammatory memory propagation in human airway epithelia
text:
People with asthma and chronic bronchitis suffer due to excessive amounts of lung mucus and persistent
inflammation, and have no available treatment options. In this proposal, we will address this problem by
studying how memory of past inflammation in lung basal stem cells may drive chronic inflammation and
excessive mucus. Findings from this proposal have great potential to improve the lives of people with
excessive mucus production due to lung disease, and may provide a basis to cure asthma.

title: PRECISE: accessible sample-to-answer RT-PCR detection of hepatitis C infection from whole blood
text:
This proposal will develop a rapid and accessible technology for HCV diagnosis by integrating sample
preparation starting with whole blood into a novel, rapid, and low-cost plasmonic thermocycling technology.
The target metrics would be the best in class among HCV nucleic-acid tests, benchmarked by the target
product profile recommended by the NOSI.

title: Examine Individual and Clinical Factors Affecting Liver Disease Management
text: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) affects approximately 2.4 million Americans, with Asian American communities experiencing higher rates of infection and liver cancer. This study will collaborate with community and clinical partners to examine factors that influence HBV screening, linkage to care, and treatment among populations at increased risk. Findings will inform the development of effective, culturally tailored strategies to improve early detection, treatment, and long-term management of chronic liver conditions.

title: GENESIS: Generative Ecosystem for Navigating Efficient Scientific Information Sharing
text:
Data sharing is crucial for accelerating scientiﬁc discoveries, especially in breast cancer research, yet researchers
are reluctant to share sensitive health data due to privacy concerns. This project introduces GENESIS, a synthetic
data generation ecosystem designed to actively facilitate data sharing while mitigating privacy risks. By introducing
new synthetic data generation methods that maintains biological constructs, clinical relevance, and casual
relationships, we can expand data accessibility to enhance our understanding of complex diseases and treatment
responses.

title: Retroviral RLI immunomodulatory gene therapy for glioblastoma
text:
Considerable preclinical and clinical evidence has emerged in recent years suggesting that the poor prognosis
faced by glioma patients is in part due to the lack of an effective antitumor T-cell response. Here, we will
investigate a localized and comprehensive approach of replicating retroviral delivery of RLI, an IL-15 fusion
protein, and other immunomodulatory genes as a therapeutic strategy for glioblastoma. Direct stimulation of an
anti-tumor T-cell mediated immune response through retroviral delivery of these genes will reverse the T-cell
poor nature of glioblastoma without systemic toxicity.

title: Role of FACT in ZFTA-RelA fusion driven ependymoma
text:
Ependymoma is the third most common malignant brain tumor in children with no effective chemotherapeutics
identified to date. We propose to thoroughly investigate FACT (FAcilitates Chromatin Transcription) as a driver
of the highly lethal ependymoma subtype, ZFTA-RELA. Results will offer preclinical insight into FACT as a
therapeutic target and establish the efficacy of CBL0137 as rationale therapy to inform future clinical trial design
for this devastating disease.

title: Neural circuits for disinhibition in the cerebellum
text:
The cerebellum's role in motor learning depends on instructive signals from climbing fibers that induce corrective
plasticity in Purkinje cells in response to motor errors. While climbing fibers directly affect Purkinje cell activity,
their interactions with molecular layer interneurons (MLIs), which strongly inhibit Purkinje cells and regulate their
response to climbing-fiber input, are not well understood; moreover, climbing fibers often fire synchronously, but
the functional significance of this synchronized activity is unknown. This study aims to elucidate how
synchronous climbing fibers activity engages different subtypes of interconnected MLIs to paradoxically promote
Purkinje cell disinhibition during motor errors in response to synchronous climbing fiber firing; such targeted
disinhibition during adaptive learning likely enhances plasticity induction, offering insights into the regulation of
instructive signaling and the broader understanding of cerebellar function in health and disease.

title: BRITE 2.0: A just-in-time adaptive intervention for suicide safety planning in adolescents
text:
Despite efforts to prevent suicide, US rates are climbing, and suicide is the second leading cause of death
amongst youth. Digital tools, especially personal smartphones, are promising avenues to address these issues
and can be used to increase engagement with effective interventions such as suicide safety planning. This
Fast-Track SBIR proposal will enhance the effectiveness of the delivery of BRITE, a suicide safety planning
smartphone application for youth at risk for suicide, by developing and testing an augmented version of the app
that will integrate just-in-time adaptive intervention features to enhance engagement with the plan and thereby
increase its effectiveness.

title: Ionizable Triazine Lipids for RNA Delivery
text:
RNA-based therapies have the potential to treat a wide variety of diseases that are traditionally
considered “undruggable,” but RNA must be stabilized and delivered into cells for it to be effective.
The goal of this project is to prepare a library of ionizable, triazine-based lipids that can be used
to package, protect, and deliver RNA into cells, and to understand how their structures affect their
activities. Ultimately, a new class of lipids will be developed to increase the therapeutic potential
of RNA.

title: Precision mapping of individualized executive networks in youth
text:
Executive function is an important domain of cognition that develops rapidly during childhood, and executive
dysfunction is associated with risk taking behaviors, a broad range of negative outcomes, and psychiatric
illness. A greater understanding of individual variation in brain networks that support executive function may
be critical for the development of personalized interventions in diverse conditions. These novel clinical
interventions would benefit the public health by reducing disability and limiting the costs to society at large.

title: Gene Delivery Core
text: Investigation of the molecular and cellular pathophysiology for hematologic diseases requires rapid and low-cost access to vector preparations, and access to large libraries of vectors and production of vectors destined to high throughput screening. Further, the successful development and testing of novel gene therapies requires access to a translational vector “pipeline” which necessitates a close interaction between basic research, research vector and clinical vector manufacturing laboratories. Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, a clinical and research institution of excellence, has developed outstanding cores to provide hematology investigators with vector support for biological studies for the genetic manipulation of cells and their translation to the clinic. This core has a track record of providing high quality “research-grade” and “clinical-scale” vector services to investigators at various stages of basic and translational research, ensuring expeditious translation to the clinic. The components of the Gene Delivery Core (GDC) that contribute to this effort are the Viral Vector Core and Vector Library Core. Each of these sub-cores are equipped with its own state-of-the-art research laboratories to allow rapid access to vector libraries and viral vector products, their evaluation in routine basic research lab studies and/or high throughput screens, and their translation to the clinic as the studies move through the translational “pipeline”. All of this effort is backed by a strong Institutional commitment to translational research and widely popular demands from users in the broad hematology field. Our objectives are to provide: (1) research scale and medium scale pilot and feasibility viral vector products and consultation on vector type and design, and (2) vector library core services including production of lentiviral shRNA and CRISPR gRNA libraries for high throughput screening. Our overall goal is to advance research and development in hematology via facilitating gene delivery, gene knock down, gene knockout or gene editing, to accelerate the rate of translation.

title: Determining the mechanisms of extracellular vesicle release, function, and clearance
text:
Determining the mechanisms of extracellular vesicle release, function, and clearance
Project Narrative
Cells release and take up extracellular vesicles during normal development as well as disease, but the in vivo
functions of extracellular vesicles are still unclear. This work aims to define how extracellular vesicle budding is
regulated, identify how they are processed after uptake, and determine their signaling and functional roles. Our
findings will provide fundamental knowledge to design approaches to induce biomarker production, develop
efficient drug delivery methods, and influence diseases from inflammation to cancer metastasis to viral spread.

title: Surveillance and Genomic Characterization of Antimicrobial Resistance in Puerto Rico's Retail Food
text:
The Surveillance and Genomic Characterization of Antimicrobial Resistance in Puerto Rico’s Retail Food
project will advance fundamental knowledge about the diversity, transmission, and genomic features of
antimicrobial-resistant (AMR) bacteria in the food supply. By integrating culture-based methods with
whole-genome sequencing and advanced sequencing technologies, this research will improve our
understanding of how resistant strains emerge and disseminate across food production and retail
environments. The findings will support efforts to reduce illness by informing public health interventions,
guiding outbreak response, and strengthening AMR surveillance capacity.
